beats.intro: Chapter eight, lesson one. Metabolism, pathways and forms of energy. [[night]]On a summer night, a firefly blinks in the dark. [[glow]]Where does that light come from? The animal has turned energy into light. That is called bioluminescence. [[push]]Let's go inside, into one cell of its glowing tail. [[factory]]A living cell is a miniature chemical factory, where thousands of reactions happen at once. It pulls energy out of food, and it uses that energy to do work.
beats.metab: [[total]]All of those reactions together have a name. Metabolism is the totality of an organism's chemical reactions. [[emerge]]And metabolism is an emergent property of life. No single molecule is alive, or has metabolism. It arises from the interactions between molecules within the cell, the way a whole orchestra makes music that no single instrument makes alone. Take the molecules out of the cell, and the metabolism is gone.
beats.pathway: Now, a factory has assembly lines. In a cell they are called metabolic pathways. [[a]]A pathway begins with a specific starting molecule, call it A. [[b]]One reaction changes it into B. [[c]]Another changes B into C. [[d]]And a third makes D, the product. [[enz]]Each of those steps is catalyzed by an enzyme, and each step has its own. Enzyme one, enzyme two, enzyme three. [[spec]]So the answer to what catalyzes each step is a specific enzyme, not one enzyme for the whole line. Three reactions, three enzymes. Think of a factory line, where each worker has exactly one job. We will keep coming back to this strip all chapter.
beats.cata: Pathways come in two kinds. [[cat]]Catabolic pathways release energy by breaking down complex molecules into simpler compounds. [[resp]]Cellular respiration is the example to remember. It is the breakdown of glucose in the presence of oxygen. [[ana]]Anabolic pathways do the opposite. They consume energy to build complex molecules from simpler ones. [[prot]]Making a protein from amino acids is anabolism. Both kinds work together: breaking down food pays for building up the cell. [[bio]]The study of how organisms manage their energy resources is called bioenergetics.
beats.q1: Quick check. Is each one catabolic, or anabolic?
beats.energy: [[cap]]So what is energy? Energy is the capacity to cause change. Some forms of energy can perform work. [[kin]]Kinetic energy is the energy of motion. [[heat]]Heat, also called thermal energy, is kinetic energy too. It is the random movement of atoms or molecules. [[pot]]Potential energy is energy that matter has because of its location or its structure. A stone held high has it because of its height. [[chem]]Chemical energy is potential energy that is available for release in a chemical reaction. It sits in the structure of molecules, like the glucose the firefly eats. And energy can be converted from one form to another. A rolling ball, jiggling molecules, a stone held high and a sugar molecule each show a different form.
beats.example: [[ledge]]Picture a ball on a high ledge. Because of where it sits, it has potential energy. [[fall]]Let it fall. The potential energy turns into kinetic energy, and the ball speeds up. On the ground it has less potential energy than it had at the top. [[climb]]To get it back up, something has to carry it. A push spends kinetic energy, and the ball gains potential energy again. [[chain]]Notice that nothing was lost from the picture: energy only changed its form. The firefly does the same kind of thing inside its cells. Chemical energy in food is released, and some of it is converted into motion, into heat, and into light.
beats.q2: Quick check. A ball falls from a high ledge. What is converted into what?
beats.wrap: To sum up. [[r1]]Metabolism is all of an organism's chemical reactions, and it emerges from molecules interacting in the cell. Reactions are organized into pathways, a specific enzyme at every step. [[r2]]Catabolic pathways release energy by breaking down. Anabolic pathways use energy to build up. And energy comes as kinetic, heat, potential and chemical, always convertible from one form to another. [[end]]Now try the practice.
